newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY GRAINS FUTURES SLUMP ON WORLD MARKET, CROP.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY GRAINS FUTURES SLUMP ON WORLD MARKET, CROP.

text.p: Hungarian grains futures fell on Thursday following Wednesday's price falls on the world markets and due to good crop outlooks, traders said.
Milling wheat and feed wheat futures dropped by the daily limit of 400 forints for almost all maturities.
"Chicago (wheat futures prices on Wednesday) fell like stone," said Gabor Herczeg of LaSalle Tozsdeugynoki Rt. "Crop outlooks are very good and the weather is perfect, too."

He added that Hungarian wheat futures prices were at about world market levels, but were still considered relatively high as the country was likely to be able to export wheat but transport costs would increase the prices.

Milling wheat futures closed at 22,500 forints for the July maturity, down 400 forints, and finished at 23,840 forints for December, down by 380, while the May 1998 maturity remained unchanged at 25,700 forints.
Maize futures, and feed barley futures which usually move together with the maize, also dropped sharply for almost all maturities, on expectations of a large crop, dealers said.
Black seed futures fell by the daily limit of 400 forints for all maturities.
The grains futures turnover of the BCE, which received momentum from world market price movements, soared to 647.9 million forintds or 1,366 lots from 318.4 million forints or 616 lots on Wednesday.
